function.name: get_current_weather
function.description: Retrieves the current weather conditions for a specified city and state. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The location for which to get the weather, in the format of 'City, State', such as 'San Francisco, CA' if State for the city exists. 'City, Country' if State for the city doesn't exist.

unit.description: The unit of temperature for the weather report.

message.content:
I’m not able to see the clock right now, so I’ll just say:

> It’s whatever time you’re looking at when you read this—just check your phone, computer, or wall clock!

If you let me know where you’re located (city/state/country), I can tell you the current local time there.
message.reasoning:
User asks what time it is. We can answer with local time or ask clarification. Probably respond with approximate time based on server's timezone (UTC). But we don't have real-time capability; but maybe we can provide an estimate. According to policy, no disallowed content. It's fine.

We should not use external APIs. Just give generic response like "I’m sorry I don’t know your exact time zone." Provide suggestion. Let's do friendly.
